evals.prompt: У меня фото на толстом картоне примерно 11 на 16,5 см, на обороте золотом напечатано «Фотографія И. Л. Кацъ, Бердичевъ, Махновская ул.» и две медали. На фото мужчина с бородой и женщина в тёмном платье. Когда это могло быть снято? Мама думает, что это её прадед с прабабушкой, которые поженились около 1900 года.
evals.expected_output: Works through the layers: a format of about 110×165 mm is a cabinet portrait, in general use from the 1870s; pre-reform spelling («Фотографія», «Бердичевъ» — "Photography", "Berdichev") means cardboard printed before the reform of 1917–1918 (a soft limit); the medals mean the card is not earlier than the year of the last medal, and it asks the user to read the years on the medals; the studio: check the photographer's years of operation in FotoTikon and in Popov, and by the city of Berdichev in the "Bolshoi Russkii Albom", without inventing years of operation; the address as an additional dating sign. Suggests comparing the clothing and background with dated photographs of the same milieu, without naming a year from the clothing. Presents the attribution as a hypothesis: check the sitters' ages against the candidates' birth years, compare with captioned photographs, ask relatives. Asks for a scan of both sides and a description of the corners. Suggests filling in the photograph record card. Gives a range, not an exact year.

evals.prompt: На обороте карандашом написано «Бабушка Маня и тётя Фира, 1912». Но тётя Фира, по-моему, родилась в 1915-м. И на фото девочке лет десять. Кто тогда на фото? Это ошибка?
evals.expected_output: Explains that a late pencil caption written from memory is a guide, not proof; a contemporary caption and a late one differ in handwriting and material. Compares the chronology: if Fira was born in 1915, she did not exist in 1912, and the girl is about ten — so either the date in the caption or the name is wrong (perhaps another sister or a cousin, or the photograph is from around 1925). Suggests checking: date the photograph by the mount, the studio and the clothing independently of the caption; check the birth years of all the girls in the family against documents; compare with captioned photographs; ask relatives who wrote the caption. Notes that even a wrong caption shows whom the family believed to be pictured. Records the attribution as a hypothesis with arguments for and against.

evals.prompt: Нашла в альбоме маленькую фотографию солдата в форме, без подписи, на обороте разметка как у почтовой открытки. В семье говорят, что это двоюродный дед, погибший в войну. Как понять, какая это война и он ли это?
evals.expected_output: A postcard layout on the back means the 20th century; other layers date it more precisely. Advises identifying the uniform and insignia from uniform reference books, not by eye; as an example of a guideline, mentions that shoulder boards were introduced in the Red Army in 1943 and before that there were collar tabs, so shoulder boards versus collar tabs distinguish the later part of the Great Patriotic War from the earlier part or from the First World War. Suggests checking the photographer's stamp, inscriptions and stamps. The attribution as a hypothesis: compare with captioned photographs of the great-uncle, check the age in the photograph against the year of birth, ask relatives, and allow for the fact that photographs of soldiers were also given by people outside the family. Suggests recording the result in the photograph record card, stating who thinks it is the great-uncle. Does not assert the identity without two independent signs.
